messages.subject: camtrapR v3: new functionality + paper in MEE
messages.subject_clean: camtrapR v3: new functionality + paper in MEE
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

the paper describing camtrapR v3 <https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210x.70409> has been published in Methods in Ecology and Evolution.

The new package version has been available for a few months already. Since many of you have been using the package for a while, here's a summary of what's new.

What's new in v3

----------------

camtrapR started out more than 11 years ago as a tool for preparing camera-trap data for analysis in other packages. V3 now extends it into an end-to-end analytical platform:

- Data import: supported formats now include exports from Wildlife Insights and datasets following the Camtrap DP standard, alongside the classic   camtrapR folder structures.

- Covariate creation: extract site-level covariates from your own local rasters or from online sources, for use in models and as input for spatial predictions.

- Exploration: A new function for creating synthetic camera trap data sets for testing. Another function for species accumulation curves.

- Accessibility: basic camtrapR data objects (camera trap table, record table, camera operation matrix, detection history) now have informative summary() and print() methods, and in some cases plot() methods, providing more meaningful summaries and more in the R console.

- Community occupancy models: Bayesian community models (via JAGS or NIMBLE) with customizable model structure, and methods for creating response plots and maps of predicted occupancy and species richness, and percentage of area occupied. Convergence diagnostics and posterior predictive checks are available for checking fitted models.

- surveyDashboard(): a new graphical interface that walks you through the entire pipeline - data import, exploration, covariates, single species and community occupancy modelling, prediction maps - without writing any code. All tools are available through a graphical interface as a Shiny app. It makes fairly advanced methods more broadly accessible and can be used for analyses of camera-trap analysis as well as teaching without the coding hurdle.

For a detailed list of changes see the package news section <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/news/news.html>.

Getting started

---------------

install.packages("camtrapR")

Note that V3 is an addition: existing scripts and workflows continue to work unchanged. New  functionality is covered in the paper <https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210x.70409>. All new functions have help files which you can access via e.g.:

?surveyDashboard

A new vignette <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/camtrapr6.html> (6: Sample camera trap datasets and the 'surveyDashboard) loads various sample data sets into the dashboard so you can get a feel for it quickly.

Feedback

--------

If you run into problems, please post here in the Google Group as usual, or open an issue on GitHub <https://github.com/jniedballa/camtrapR/issues>.

And if there's functionality you'd like to see, I'd genuinely like to hear about it. Feature requests now have a proper home in the GitHub discussions <https://github.com/jniedballa/camtrapR/discussions>, but you can also use this Google Group as usual.

Thank you for using camtrapR.

Best,

Jürgen Niedballa
